- When sentiment is negative and forecast is trending up, reduce forecasted values by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in upward moves.
- When sentiment is positive and forecast is trending down, increase forecasted values by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.
- Avoid forecasting sharp spikes in price after recent highs — model tends to overreact; cap upward revisions at 10% of prior peak.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from negative to positive), delay forecast adjustment for 2–3 periods to allow market to confirm trend.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is 10%+ above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2–5% per period; if below, increase by 2–5% per period.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid forecasting values > 15% above 30-day moving average — often overestimates volatility.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model tends to underpredict downside — add 3–5% buffer to downward forecasts.
- Forecast corrections should be applied only after 3–5 consecutive days of sentiment alignment with price direction.
